qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Monopolistic surface ownership of ~873,000 contiguous and checkerboard acres across the core Delaware and Midland Basins, coupled with >200,000 Net Royalty Acres. Receives perpetual ad valorem gross production royalties and high-margin water sourcing/produced water disposal fees without bearing any drilling capital or operating expenditure. Proof of moat is demonstrated by 10-year median ROIC of ~38.5% (FY24 ~49.7%, FY25 ~33%) and sustained 80-90% operating margins. Primary erosion risks are long-term basin resource depletion and severe commodity price collapses.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Remarkable ~85-90% operating margin Permian land and royalty business with zero drilling capex, but Upstream Energy baseline persistence is Tier 4 (5-10Y baseline CAP). Faces active unhedged terminal headwinds under Macrotrend [4] (Energy Transition & Resource Limits) from secular peak hydrocarbon demand, electrification, and finite Permian Tier 1 well inventory depletion over a 15-30 year horizon.
qualitative.evidence: Texas Pacific Land Corporation (TPL) holds ~873,000 surface acres and over 200,000 Net Royalty Acres in the Permian Basin (Delaware and Midland Basins). Revenues derive from oil & gas royalties (~55-60%), Water Services and Operations (~35-40%), and surface easements/materials (~5%). Financial efficiency is exceptional: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 38.5% (FY24 ROIC ~49.7%, FY25 ROIC ~33%), operating margins exceed 80-85%, FCF conversion is ~95-100%, and the balance sheet carries minimal long-term debt with positive net cash/equivalents ($145M-$370M). However, under the Mauboussin industry persistence framework, Upstream Energy is anchored at Tier 4 (p=0.70-0.71, baseline CAP 5-10 years), and the business model is inherently tied to finite fossil fuel extraction and regional Permian drilling activity, failing Gate 4's 15-year secular resilience requirement.
